Caveats, no code change. The paper prints no count at assignment or per arm, so balance cannot be checked. Of 852 enrollees, 758 completed, and the text does not say whether the dropouts had been randomized. The main phase ran through 'a link' sent weeks after enrollment, and the paper describes no check that control subjects did not use AI on their own. The form records the count gaps.

confirmed.statement: The file is the working paper dated September 22, 2023 (HBS WP 24-013). I could not check the assignment text of the Organization Science (2026) version of record.

summary: The PDF supports every part of the assignment, arms, and ai_tool coding for S1 and S2: after a no-AI baseline task, individual BCG consultants were randomly assigned, with stratification, to no AI, a GPT-4 chat platform, or the same platform plus a prompt-engineering overview (abstract, PDF p. 4; Methods, PDF pp. 10-12), and in S1 they used it to write their own shoe-product ideas. The open issues leave criterion 1 intact, and the form already records most of them: no counts at assignment or per arm, unclear timing of the 852-to-758 attrition, no stated check on AI use in the control arm, a fixed-order before-after comparison that the form marks as not randomized, and a 2023 working paper in place of the 2026 version of record.
